title: Latency insights panel: model + route breakdown with streaming vs sync splits
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Background: SRE and product teams keep asking for a single-pane view that shows latency percentiles broken down by both model and API route, with explicit differentiation of streaming vs non-streaming requests. Current dashboards show endpoint latencies but mix streaming and non-streaming requests and do not surface time-to-first-byte (TTFB) vs total completion time. That makes it hard to diagnose regressions that affect streaming tails (token emission) vs synchronous completion paths (model decode + compilation).

Goal: Build a new dashboard panel (and supporting telemetry) that surfaces p50/p95/p99 by model and route, with two orthogonal splits: 1) streaming vs non-streaming, and 2) TTFB vs total completion time. The panel should be usable by PMs/SEs during incidents and for periodic quality/cost reviews. It must be backed by deterministic metrics and traces so rows can link to a representative trace or logs.

Scope & deliverables:
- Telemetry: instrument and emit two histogram metrics from inference runtime: inference_time_ms{model,route,is_streaming,model_version,status} and time_to_first_byte_ms{model,route,is_streaming,model_version,status}. Use histogram buckets tuned for 1ms-60s range.
- Tracing: add span hooks in request router and decoder to attach attributes: route, model, model_version, is_streaming, batch_size, cache_hit. Ensure these appear in Tempo/Jaeger. Sampling: keep current 1% global sampling but increase to 5% for requests that exceed p95 to help tail debugging.
- Logging pipeline: ensure request_id and trace_id propagate to logs; update log schema to include is_streaming and model_version for correlating dashboards to logs in Loki/Elasticsearch.
- Dashboard: Grafana panel with table and heatmap views: rows grouped by model+route, columns for p50/p95/p99 for TTFB and completion time, and a small sparkline of trend. Toggle to compare streaming vs non-streaming. Drill-down links to representative trace and the request-level log search.
- Alerts: add an SLO-derived alert for model-route pairs that exceed a rolling p99 threshold for >10 minutes (configurable).

Non-goals: this ticket does not implement query-level APM or per-token latency breakdown for autoregressive models (separate follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Backend emits the two histograms (inference_time_ms and time_to_first_byte_ms) with labels: model, route, is_streaming, model_version, status
Tracing hooks include attributes route, model, model_version, is_streaming and traces for >p95 requests are sampled at 5%
Dashboard shows p50/p95/p99 for both TTFB and completion time grouped by model+route and supports streaming vs non-streaming toggle
Each model+route row has a link that opens a representative trace and a pre-filled log query for the same time range
Dashboard queries execute within 10s for a 1h time window (perf target); queries use pre-aggregated Prometheus histograms or aggregated backend metrics to avoid scanning raw logs
Runbook updated with how to interpret streaming vs non-streaming spikes and escalation steps

implementation_notes:
Tradeoffs: computing p99 in Prometheus histograms is approximate; we rely on Prometheus summary for short windows and pre-aggregated histograms for long windows to keep query latency low. Streaming TTFB is measured at first decoder token emission, which captures server production but may include network-induced chunking delays for certain clients — add client-side instrumentation later. We intentionally keep is_streaming as a boolean label; if we need more granularity (partial vs full-stream), create a follow-up.

Deployment plan: emit metrics behind a feature flag, validate in canary (10% traffic) for 48h, then flip globally. Dashboard will point to canary metrics with a toggle to production namespace. Alert thresholds will be off by default until baseline collected for two weeks.

Open questions: exact histogram bucket boundaries (proposed exponential 1,2,5,10,20,50,100,200,500,1000,2000,5000,10000,30000,60000 ms) and whether to collapse model_version label in dashboards for readability.
